items.markdown:
If you’re looking around Manchester, I’d start with **The Royal Kennel Club’s puppy-finder** rather than buying from a general classified advert. Its current Staffordshire Bull Terrier search shows blue litters, including one in Smethwick, although availability changes quickly. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

A local search also turns up businesses such as IDCBULLZ MANCHESTER and [Bonosue](http://www.bonosue.co.uk/) in Bolton, but I would **not treat a business listing or reviews as proof that a breeder is responsible**. Verify the breeder and litter independently.

### What to ask the breeder

For a Staffy, these are the questions I'd put at the top of your list:

- **Can I see the puppy with its mother, at the place where it was raised?** Don't agree to meet in a car park or have the puppy delivered to you.
- **Can I see the mother's and father's health-test certificates/results?** For Staffordshire Bull Terriers, the Royal Kennel Club recommends testing for **HC-HSF4 hereditary cataracts and L-2-HGA**, plus **elbow testing and eye testing/litter eye screening**. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/BreedSpecificRequirements?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **What are the parents' actual results, rather than simply "health tested"?** Ask to see the certificates and check the registered dogs yourself.
- **What is the parents' inbreeding coefficient, and can I see their KC records?**
- **Has the puppy had a veterinary examination, vaccinations, microchip and worming?**
- **How have the puppies been socialised?** Ask specifically about children, household noises, handling, other dogs and being left alone. PDSA also recommends asking breeders about early socialisation. [PDSA](https://www.pdsa.org.uk/pet-help-and-advice/looking-after-your-pet/puppies-dogs/medium-dogs/staffordshire-bull-terrier?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Can I see the puppy's paperwork before paying a deposit?**
- **Will you take the dog back or help rehome it if I can't keep it later?**
- **How many litters does the mother have, and how old is she?**
- **Why did you choose these two dogs to breed?** A good breeder should be able to explain the health and temperament reasoning, not just talk about colour or appearance.

### Be particularly careful about "blue"

Blue is actually a **breed-standard colour** for Staffordshire Bull Terriers, so there's nothing inherently wrong with wanting a blue Staffy. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

But I'd be wary of a breeder heavily marketing *"rare blue," "exclusive blue,"* or unusually high prices. The Royal Kennel Club explicitly says **health and temperament should take priority over colour**. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Also, don't accept "KC registered" as equivalent to "health tested." Those are separate things.
